title: Sleep and Circadian Modifiers of ADHD and Bipolar-Spectrum Functioning
background: This module evaluates whether sleep duration, sleep quality, circadian irregularity, and shift work modify attention, executive functioning, irritability, mood, and mania risk.
population: Adolescents and adults with ADHD, bipolar-spectrum disorder, both conditions, or relevant control groups.
intervention: Short sleep, sleep deprivation, insomnia, circadian disruption, irregular sleep, delayed sleep phase, or shift work.
comparator: Adequate or regular sleep, euthymia, non-shift work, within-person baseline, or unexposed controls.

outcomes_primary.name: Attention, executive function, irritability, and real-world functioning
Hypomanic, manic, mixed, or psychotic symptoms and mood instability

outcomes_secondary.name: Temporal direction, within-person effects, and reverse causation

inclusion: Adolescent or adult ADHD or bipolar-spectrum sample, or a study directly relevant to differential diagnosis.
Measures sleep duration, quality, circadian timing, irregularity, insomnia, or shift work.
Reports cognitive, functional, mood, mania, psychosis, or irritability outcomes.
Empirical study or authoritative evidence synthesis.
exclusion: Sleep-treatment efficacy study without information on sleep as a modifier.
No separable ADHD or bipolar-spectrum result and no direct differential-diagnosis relevance.
Opinion or protocol without empirical results.
No outcome relevant to claim H7.

analysis.effect_measure: Narrative synthesis separating trait, state, and temporal-direction evidence.

registration: Protocol frozen for AI-assisted rapid review on 2026-07-29; not prospectively registered.
disclaimer: AI Reviewer-1 rapid-review draft. Human Reviewer 2 and clinical sign-off remain pending. Not diagnostic or treatment guidance.
